messages:
alex: Heads up — we're seeing a tail-latency cluster in eu-west between 22:10-22:25. Correlates with big embedding jobs. Dashboard: https://dash.re/redwood/eu-west/p2p

maria: Metrics show PCIe P2P read stalls spiking to 180-220ms on r4-*/gpu nodes, p2p tx bytes at 92%+. NIC utilization not the limiting factor, looks like PCIe saturation.

sam: Is it isolated to one tenant or multiple?

jess: Two large embedding tenants (t-emb1, t-emb2) doing dense KV pulls, plus several small chat jobs — the embeddings pattern causes many cross-GPU DMA ops.

alex: So noisy neighbor but at the PCIe layer. Short-term mitigation: we should gate P2P DMA windows per-tenant (soft caps) instead of whole-node eviction. Proposal: implement a scheduler-level token bucket for P2P ops (p2p-credit). If tenant exhausts tokens, route to compatible quantized/replica model or delay their batch window a few 10s ms.

maria: We can also add an eBPF NIC qdisc to smooth bursts, but that doesn't fix PCIe DMA stalls. Agree token approach seems more surgical.

sam: Implementation options: (1) runtime-level token check before issuing P2P memcpy, (2) kernel driver hack to limit peer-to-peer bar reads, (3) scheduler backpressure delaying batches. (1) lowest blast radius.

jess: Runtime change needed anyway for batching KV pulls locally + coalescing — that reduces P2P by ~60% in perf tests. Can we do a hybrid: runtime token check + batching?

alex: Hybrid sounds good. For rollout: canary in eu-west with 10% headroom reserved for P2P (i.e., tokens preallocated to system/background), and p2p-credit enabled on 2 rack pools. If tokens hit limit, router will fall back to quantized model variant.

maria: Quick command to toggle canary feature:
```
# enable p2p credits for tenant t-emb1 with 50 tokens per second window
rdctl p2p-credit set --tenant t-emb1 --tokens 50 --window 1s --pool euw-canary
```

sam: Can we measure cost impact? Reserving headroom reduces peak GPU fill — rough calc: +6% reserved capacity needed on canary to keep SLOs. Need to run cost-vs-SLO sim.

jess: I ran a sim yesterday: for 2 heavy tenants, SLO misses drop from 3.1% -> 0.4% while utilization drops by ~5%. Worth it for critical customers.

alex: Ok action plan:
- enable p2p-credit canary in eu-west (maria)
- runtime token-check + batching patch PR (jess)
- router fallback rule to quantized variant when tokens exhausted (sam)
- cost sim update and stakeholder note to pricing (alex)

maria: I'll flip the canary now. Deploy-bot will post status.

deploy-bot: Applied p2p-credit policy to pool euw-canary -> pools: r4-a[rack1], r4-a[rack2]. Monitoring: https://dash.re/redwood/eu-west/p2p-canary. :white_check_mark:

alex: Nice. Monitor logs for KV fetch latencies and PCIe stall counters. If no regressions after 30m, expand to other racks.

sam: Also flag to infra-costs for the +5-6% reserved headroom — need approval for monthly committed allocation change if we expand.

jess: I'll open the PR and mark it for review. TL;DR: surgical p2p token gating + batching reduces noisy neighbor PCIe stalls with small utilization hit.

alex: Thanks all. We'll reconvene in 45m for status. :thumbsup:
